messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High error rate fetching model artifacts from Hugging Face (HTTP 429) observed across multiple hosts; cold-start model pulls failing. Alert: 15% artifact fetch failures in last 5m. Check monitor: https://alerts.redwood.ai/INC-2098. Investigating.

Samar Singh: Seeing the same in prod logs — repeated 429 from huggingface artifact URLs during model startup. Affected model families: gpt-small-v1, llama-3-7b-q8. Warm instances serving cached KV are OK, but scale-up results in rollout failures. Error snippet from inference node logs: `blob fetch failed: 429 Too Many Requests`

June Park: I'm on infra oncall, taking lead. Acknowledging pager. I'll scope blast radius and start mitigation steps. @Miguel Diaz can you try contacting HF SRE? :phone:

Miguel Diaz: Reached out to HF support, created ticket HF-12345 and DM'd their SRE channel. HF status page shows elevated rate limiting in artifact CDN region eu-central. Link: https://status.huggingface.co/ — they confirm throttling due to increased traffic. I've posted request for temporary rate increases; no ETA yet.

Ryan Chen: To reduce new cold-starts we can do a quick routing change to use our S3 mirror for those specific model versions if the artifacts exist. Commands to flip registry override: ```bash
# temporary registry override to mirror
rdctl config set artifact.registry_override 's3://redwood-artifact-mirror/hf'
rdctl rollout --service inference --selector region=eu --force
```

Samar Singh: We only have a subset mirrored. For models without mirror we should enable a fallback variant (quantized smaller) to keep requests alive. Also reduce concurrent fetches to HF to avoid retry storms. I'll open a PR to change fetch concurrency and add exponential backoff cap.

June Park: Rolling a targeted canary: route 10% of cold-starts to "fallback-small-quant" variant and keep 90% on normal rollout while mirror flip happens. Canary policy JSON: ```json
{
  "route": "model.load",
  "percent": 10,
  "fallback_variant": "gpt-small-v1-quant-fallback"
}
``` Applying to eu region now.

oncall-bot: Pager acknowledged by Miguel Diaz. Escalation sent to @ML-Infra. :arrow_up:

ML-Infra: Investigating runtime retry and batching. Immediate actions: (1) throttle parallel artifact pulls per-host to 2, (2) cap retry window to 30s with increasing backoff, (3) enable local ephemeral cache TTL extension to keep warmed artifacts longer. Pushing config change now.

Elaine (CSM): Flagging impacted customers — AcmeCorp and BetaApps have reported increased error rates in the last hour. I'll notify support and the account teams, prepare a short incident note we can send to those contacts.

Samar Singh: Customer impact summary for status: "Degraded artifact fetches from Hugging Face intermittent 429s causing prolonged cold-start times and occasional model load failures. Warm instances unaffected. Mitigations in flight: routing to mirror, fallback model canary, and download concurrency limits." Please review before posting.

Miguel Diaz: HF responded: they are applying a regional throttle relaxation in ~20-30m and suggested reducing burst traffic. They asked us to reduce parallel pulls per IP. I've added the parallelism cap and triggered the mirror switch for mirrored models. Rolling out now.

June Park: Mirror switch is live for ~40% of affected versions in eu. Canary to fallback variant is active. Early metrics: artifact failures down from 15% -> 6% in the last 5m for canaried traffic. Continuing monitoring for 30m.

oncall-bot: Incident update logged. Initial mitigation applied; team will monitor and update every 10 minutes. Incident owner: Miguel Diaz. Tags: third-party:huggingface, severity:high, impact:cold-starts.

Samar Singh: Follow-ups: (1) add permanent mirror coverage plan for high-usage models, (2) add pre-warm strategy for new deployments, (3) document fetch concurrency defaults to avoid hammering 3p registries. I'll draft RFC after incident stabilizes.

Elaine (CSM): I'll prepare customer communication template and coordinate once we have a clearer ETA from HF. :thumbsup:
